stem: Sana uses a circuit tester with a cell, a bulb, and wires. She joins a graphite pencil lead between the free ends and the bulb glows. She then joins a rubber eraser between the free ends and the bulb stays off.

options.text: The graphite pencil lead is a good conductor; the rubber eraser is a poor conductor.
The graphite pencil lead is a poor conductor; the rubber eraser is a good conductor.
Both materials are good conductors because Sana used the same tester each time.
Both materials are poor conductors because only metals can ever glow a tester bulb.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A glowing bulb shows the pencil lead lets current through; a bulb that stays off shows the eraser does not.

teacher.key_rationale: Glow means the joined material conducts; no glow means it does not. Graphite conducts; rubber does not. B reverses the labels; C and D ignore the different bulb outcomes.
